title: Responses v6: frame-level streaming, RNG-hint forwarding, and metadata attribute routing for OpenAI compatibility
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Add Responses v6 framing and RNG-hint passthrough to OpenAI bridge; clients using new `seed_hint` or attribute-routing can opt into deterministic hints and richer per-chunk metadata. Backwards compatible with legacy OpenAI adapters.
description:
Motivation: OpenAI introduced a Responses v6-style streaming frame model that emits richer per-frame attributes and explicit RNG/determinism hints. Customers integrating via the OpenAI compatibility bridge have asked for (1) stable streaming reassembly when frames are split differently by proxies, (2) a simple passthrough for RNG/determinism hints (seed_hint) so users can opt into reproducible generation, and (3) a flexible attribute routing mechanism so arbitrary metadata fields from the Responses frames can be surfaced to Redwood response objects and audit logs.

This PR implements a compatibility layer that: 1) introduces frame-level IDs and mapping logic so the bridge can reassemble out-of-order or chunked frames without altering token order; 2) forwards `seed_hint` and `determinism` attributes from upstream frames into the internal Response attributes and the SDK-facing response metadata (preserving the original hint string); 3) provides an attribute-routing config with field mappings and allow/deny lists so teams can opt into passthrough of fields like `tool_call_context`, `response_flags`, and customer-supplied `meta.*` keys; 4) maintains legacy behavior unless the `openai_compat=v6` flag is set in the request or tenant config.

Implementation notes: - Bridge: new frame-mapper module that consumes incoming frame envelopes and produces reassembly events. Reassembly is streaming-friendly and emits partial reassembled frames if a gap persists for configurable timeout. - Attributes: `seed_hint` and `determinism` are copied into `response.metadata.seed_hint` and `response.metadata.determinism_level`. We preserve the verbatim source value and annotate the response with `compat.openai_v6=true`. - Routing: added `openai.attribute_route` config (string->string list) in the bridge config. Route examples are in docs. - Tool-calls: when a frame contains `tool_call` attributes split across several frames, the frame-mapper ensures tool-call payloads are reassembled before the SDK receives the structured tool object; partial tool-call fragments are buffered up to 5s by default. - Tests: end-to-end harness simulates chunked network boundaries, reordered frames, and mixed v5/v6 upstreams. New unit tests cover mapping edge cases and attribute mappings.

Checklist: - [x] frame mapper module and unit tests - [x] attribute passthrough config and tests - [x] SDK shim updates to expose seed_hint in Python/TS SDKs - [x] e2e harness for chunk reassembly - [x] migration docs and examples - [x] performance microbenchmarks (no measurable latency regression in 95th percentile for typical small chat workloads)

Related: ENG-8921 (feature work), SUP-4187 (customer ask), docs: #doc-openai-bridge-v6 in the internal docs space.

Notes on backwards compatibility and opt-in: Default behavior remains unchanged for tenants that have not enabled the compat flag. The new reassembly logic is conservative: only applies mapping for requests marked `openai_compat=v6` or for requests that contain an explicit `frame_version: "v6"` envelope. This reduces risk for older clients that rely on current streaming framing.

Operational considerations: - There is a small additional memory cost for buffering partial frames during reassembly; we add a configurable cap (default 3MB per request) and an eviction policy with a diagnostic metric `bridge.reassembly.evicted_frames_count`. - Metric and tracing: added `bridge.frame_mapper.latency_ms` and span annotations for reassembly events. - Observability: Console exposes a table of routed attributes per-request for customers who enable detailed logging.

Rollout plan: staged rollout by tenant flag, start with internal infra and a small canary group for Dedicated customers, then open to self-serve tenants. Monitor `bridge.frame_mapper.errors` and `sdk.openai_compat.seed_hint_usage` for the first 2 weeks.

If you want to test quickly: use the `tools/resp-v6-sim` script that emits reordered frames and optionally attaches `seed_hint: "s-1234"`. Example request header: `X-Redwood-Compat: openai_v6`.
commits: feat(bridge): add frame-mapper for v6 streaming reassembly
feat(bridge): forward seed_hint and determinism attributes into response.metadata
feat(config): attribute routing config and validation
fix(sdk): expose response.metadata.seed_hint in python and ts SDKs
test(harness): add e2e chunk reassembly scenarios
docs: document openai v6 attribute routing and rollout steps
review_comments: Owen Patel: Nice approach to buffering — can we make the default buffer timeout configurable per-tenant? I think 5s is fine but ops may want shorter defaults.
Marisol Vega: @Owen yes, made it configurable via `openai.reassembly.timeout_ms` with a 5s default; updated docs.
Rina Chen: Are we validating attributes size to prevent huge passthrough fields from being stored? Please add a defensive limit.
Marisol Vega: Added a 64KB-per-attribute soft limit with metric `bridge.attribute.truncated_count` and documented behavior.
Diego Morales: CI flaked on the e2e harness due to a race — I suggested a deterministic seed for the simulator. After that tests passed.
CI Bot: build/pipeline passed after a rerun. Coverage decreased by 0.2% but all new code is covered by unit and e2e tests.
